transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-12-07
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~45 minutes
- Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Rachel Kim (Lumen Eng Mgr), Daniel Ortiz (Lumen Sr Eng), Priya Singh (Lumen Security)

Summary:
Quick SDK integration walkthrough focused on Python/TypeScript quickstarts, auth flow (API keys vs. OIDC/SAML), env setup for dedicated vs hosted, and a proposed 1-week benchmark for latency/cost. Customer is evaluating hosted API for initial pilot but wants private deployment options for PHI-sensitive flows.

Topics:
- SDK quickstart (Python + TS)
- Auth and environment variables, KMS & key rotation
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs (latency, cost, data residency)
- Benchmarks and pilot plan
- Security/compliance docs and next steps

Transcript:
00:00 - Sofia Martinez: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're excited to walk through the SDKs today, quick agenda is python+ts quickstarts, auth, env setup and then q&a, sound good?
00:07 - Rachel Kim: yea that works for us, thanks Sofia, we have about 30 minutes to go over tech then a followup for sec with Priya
00:13 - Arjun Patel: cool i'll share my screen, bear with me, so first quickstart - python - pip install redwood-inference, set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var, then from redwood import Client, response = client.generate(...) - small snippet, error handling notes
00:32 - Daniel Ortiz: is there a typed client for TS too, like for node?
00:36 - Arjun Patel: absolutely, npm i @redwood/inference, then import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference', const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }) - we also support browser flows but recommend server-side for secrets
00:49 - Rachel Kim: quick q on auth, we have an internal policy requiring short lived creds and KMS rotation, how are keys managed with hosted?
00:56 - Sofia Martinez: great q. for hosted you get API keys that can be rotated via console or API; we also support customer-managed keys via KMS for Private, and we have guidance for short-lived tokens using OIDC exchange. Arjun do you want to show the sample code?
01:10 - Arjun Patel: yeah, show the oidc flow - it's basically: exchange your OIDC token at /v1/auth/exchange -> get short lived token, set as Authorization bearer, fallback to apikeys for simple setups, note the SDK has helpers to refresh tokens, small snippet here, um code sample link: https://redwood.example/docs/sdk-auth (link shared in chat)
01:33 - Priya Singh: on KMS - when you say customer-managed, is that specifically AWS KMS? we use an internal HSM for keys, need to check compliance
01:40 - Arjun Patel: we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and have an HSM workflow for Private deployments; for hosted we can support envelope encryption with a customer key in some tiers, for Private you keep full control. we'll send the security pack with details
01:55 - Daniel Ortiz: latency question - our p50 needs to be under 200ms for short prompts, do you have benchmarks for your hosted infra?
02:02 - Sofia Martinez: typical p50 for our curated open models is 120-220ms depending on model and seq length; for dedicated you can tune instance types and kernel/quantization to hit target; Arjun has run internal tests, Arjun?
02:14 - Arjun Patel: yep, for 2k token seq we see p50 ~180ms on A100 pooled serving, if you need consistent <200ms at scale dedicated pools with pinned capacity are best. note tradeoffs: dedicated = higher base cost but stable latency and isolation.
02:31 - Rachel Kim: when you mention pooling does that preserve KV cache across requests? our app uses streaming chat with recency, want cache retained per session
02:39 - Arjun Patel: good call - we do KV/prefix caching strategies, you can pin session ids and we can persist kv cache for the session lifetime in Dedicated. in hosted we have sticky routing and short TTLs, but for guaranteed persistence we'd recommend Dedicated or Private with an attached cache store.
02:56 - Priya Singh: data residency - we need EU-only for PHI, do you have region pinning?
03:02 - Sofia Martinez: yes region pinning for model serving and data residency is supported; for Private we can deploy into your VPC in eu-west-1 or on-prem. we'll include a doc for deployment patterns.
03:12 - Daniel Ortiz: ok back to SDKs, how do we handle batching and async generation in the client? our throughput is ~200 req/s in spikes
03:20 - Arjun Patel: SDK has a batching helper and async methods; you can configure batch window, max tokens per batch, and concurrency. for spikes we recommend queueing + autoscaling on Dedicated; our console shows token-level breakdowns to tune batching.
03:38 - Rachel Kim: show us the typescript quickstart real quick?
03:41 - Arjun Patel: switching - here's a quick demo, code snippet run, playwright flubbed my copy but gist in chat, imports, simple generate call, streaming example with onToken callback, error handling for 429s, exponential backoff sample
04:10 - Daniel Ortiz: about cost - we need per-token economics to estimate monthly spend - can you share a sample calc?
04:17 - Sofia Martinez: yes we will share a pricing sheet - hosted per-token + embeddings; Dedicated is node-based pricing with commit and overage; we'll tailor the pilot pricing for Lumen, send as part of next steps
04:27 - Priya Singh: any SOC2, ISO certs? we need audit logs and RBAC for compliance
04:33 - Sofia Martinez: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II compliant and has ISO in progress, we provide audit logs in Console, RBAC and SSO (SAML/OIDC). we'll attach the security pack; Arjun will include architecture diagram and sample network policy
04:47 - Rachel Kim: ok for the benchmark, what metrics do you want? we'll provide request traces and a sample dataset
04:53 - Arjun Patel: ideal: p50/p95 latency, tokens per second, model used, cold vs warm cache, CPU/GPU utilization, error rates, cost per 1k tokens. provide a representative traffic file and we'll run a 1-week window on Dedicated or Hosted equivalent env
05:06 - Daniel Ortiz: how intrusive is integration for our backend? our stack is go + node microservices, dockerized
05:12 - Arjun Patel: minimal - SDKs are lightweight; for serverside we recommend using backend services to call Redwood and not embed keys in frontends, use OIDC for service accounts. container examples in the quickstart repo.
05:25 - Rachel Kim: any blockers for us to trial hosted first then shift to Private?
05:29 - Sofia Martinez: no blockers; common flow is start hosted pilot, evaluate quality/cost, then move to Dedicated or Private for PHI. we also support snapshots for model versions when migrating.
05:40 - Priya Singh: can we get an architectural diagram for Private with our HSM?
05:44 - Arjun Patel: yes we'll send a sample topology with HSM integration and network flow.
05:50 - Sofia Martinez: recap - we'll send pricing + pilot terms, security pack, SDK quickstart links, and schedule benchmark window. Suggested follow up week of 12/14 for Private deep dive.
05:59 - Rachel Kim: thanks all, that's helpful, Daniel will send traffic file, Priya will review security doc, we'll reconvene next week
06:06 - Sofia Martinez: awesome thanks everyone, talk soon

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-heard words, some speaker overlaps; code snippets summarized rather than exact copy-paste. Links shared in chat: https://redwood.example/docs/sdk-quickstart, https://redwood.example/docs/security-pack, pricing-sheet (link to be emailed).
